plates.head: A swarm of AI agents that runs businesses on its own.
lines: Applied AI software that does the work of a business, not another tool for it. Raising a $2M seed.

plates.head: The owner does the work only they can do. AMTECH's agents do everything else.
lines: The owner does the work only they can do. AMTECH's agents do everything else.

AMTECH is an applied AI company building autonomous agent swarms for businesses. A swarm sets itself up in minutes, works around the clock and costs about $2 a day to run. It is software that does the work, not software someone has to run. We take it to market one focused beachhead at a time, starting with real estate, construction and the trades.

plates.head: Every business will run on AI agents. Almost none can set them up.
lines: Running agents is a job of its own. Pick the models, build the infrastructure, write the rules, connect them to the business's software, and manage them every day.
And it changes every week. New models, new tools, new practice. Owners have no time to keep up, and no one on staff who can.
So they keep paying for the old way: a stack of software subscriptions, people to run it, or a chatbot that can't do the job.

plates.head: A few questions in. A custom swarm out, in 50 to 90 seconds.
lines: The owner describes the business. AMTECH picks the agents, skills, software, pages and connections it needs.
A main agent leads a team, each agent with its own computer, accounts, budget and routines.
It runs on its own, day and night, inside the software the business already uses, and asks before anything leaves it.
The owner just talks to it, like a person. It costs about $2 a day to run.

plates.head: One platform, four industries. $4,800 a month, all signed this month.
lines: Scoop Dogg: An autonomous AI employee system runs the business, from its website and bookings to its customers.
Brand Box: Eight online stores, each with its own team of agents, under one main agent.
Weiss-Khan: Email lead generation: agents that find and enrich leads at volume.
A crypto trading desk: An agent team that trades, sizes positions and reports to the owner, around the clock.

Each pays $1,200 a month, and each swarm was made by the same engine from a few questions. And our own go-to-market runs the same way: this week our agents built and launched an autonomous sales funnel for a new industry in about three hours.

plates.head: The hard part isn't building an agent. It's running hundreds of them.
lines: Swarm orchestration: one main agent directs teams of agents, each with its own computer, accounts, budget and routines.
A metered gateway routes every call to the fastest, cheapest open-source model that can do the job, and bills it to the right customer.
The employee factory: a plain description of a business becomes a working swarm in 52 to 92 seconds, measured across stores, dental, law, agencies and contractors.
Owned data: every business it runs adds prices, leads and outcomes no competitor can buy. All proprietary code, held as trade secrets.

plates.head: Software is starting to do the work, not just hold it.
lines: Service as software. The money businesses spend on people and services is far bigger than what they spend on software. AI agents can now do much of that work.
The money is already moving. Thrive Holdings raised over $2B, and General Catalyst set aside $1.5B, to buy service businesses and run them with AI.
Every owner needs the same leverage, without selling their business or hiring an AI team.
Sequoia Capital, "Services: the new software", March 2026. Thrive Holdings and General Catalyst: press, 2025-2026.

plates.head: A new category, a focused beachhead, and the share we need.
lines: A new category 36M: US businesses pay people and services to do work that software can now do itself. That is service as software.
Our beachhead 4.3M: owners in property and the trades: 1.44M Realtors and 2.9M one-person construction businesses, in a $2.16 trillion industry.
By the end of 2027 $630K: in monthly recurring revenue ($7.6M ARR) from 3,400 businesses. Under 0.1% of the beachhead.
$100M in ARR takes about 7,000 owners on our $1,200 plan, fewer than 1 in 600. Then come the industries where we already have paying customers: online stores, lead generation and trading.
US Small Business Administration, Office of Advocacy. National Association of Realtors, June 2026. US Census Bureau: Nonemployer Statistics 2022; Value of Construction Put in Place 2025.

plates.head: AI is creating a new generation of wealth. Much of it ends up in property.
lines: New money is being made fast: at the AI labs, chipmakers and cloud companies, and in thousands of $1-10M online businesses that one person now runs with AI. That money buys homes, builds and renovates.
The crowd's bet is that AI can't do the trades. AI won't swing the hammer. It runs the business around it: sales, quotes, scheduling, follow-up and books. That's where the margin is.
We know this market. The founder's own experience and data from it, and the most owner-run, lead-driven businesses of any industry.
Competition gets harder from here. More capital chases the same jobs, and private equity is buying service businesses to run them with AI. Independent owners need the same leverage, without selling.

A signal of where this goes: in July 2026 Delaware proposed the Artificial Intelligence Company, a new kind of legal entity whose day-to-day affairs are run by an AI agent. It is still a draft, and AMTECH does not depend on it.

plates.head: A full office staff, for less than a part-time hire.
lines: 24/7: Every lead answered in seconds, nights and weekends included. No missed calls, no cold leads.
$1,200: a month for the AI employee, against $3,750 or more a month for one office hire.
0: new software for the owner to learn. The swarm works inside the tools they already use, and they talk to it like a person.
More jobs won, more margin kept, evenings back. And as they grow, the swarm grows with them, not the payroll.
Office hire: AMTECH estimate for a full-time office administrator at about $45,000 a year before benefits.

plates.head: The engine is built. Now we go deep in one vertical.
lines: Self-serve is the engine. A plain description of a business becomes a working swarm, with its team, pages, records and connections, in 52 to 92 seconds. Every customer we've set up was built on it.

Close relationships first, on purpose. Interviewing our first customers ourselves gave us more insight, more revenue and happier customers. Every interview leads to the $1,200 plan, and the $50 self-serve plan is live.
Now, autonomous go-to-market. As of this week our own agent swarms find, check, reach and follow up with owners, niche by niche.

Our beachhead: contractors, real estate agents, wholesalers and property managers, one niche at a time, each with its own offer, pages, content and outreach. The same engine then opens the next industry.

plates.head: Our go-to-market is a swarm too. Outreach and fulfillment run on their own.
lines: Outreach The outreach swarm: Finds owners niche by niche, researches each business, writes a personal free check of how it is found, then emails, calls and follows up.
Fulfillment The fulfillment swarm: Builds each customer's swarm in 50 to 90 seconds, onboards them, watches it work and improves it every week.
Content Viral content swarms: Short and long video for every niche, made by our own agent swarms for very little.
Pages A page per niche and city: Thousands of pages for every trade and town, written for Google and AI search.
Self-serve In every funnel: Any page, email or video can end in a working swarm in about a minute.
Partners Brokerages and suppliers: Brokerages, trade associations, supply houses and franchises. One deal brings hundreds of owners.
Operators Private equity: A swarm for every company in a roll-up, at 8% of revenue. One deal brings dozens of businesses.
Paid AI search and Google ads: Ads in each service area, aimed at owners looking for help.

plates.head: Private equity is buying service businesses to run them with AI. Every one needs a swarm.
lines: The money is moving into our beachhead. General Catalyst set aside $1.5B for AI roll-ups, and its Long Lake has bought dozens of HOA and property management companies. Thrive Holdings agreed in October to buy ADT, the home security company.
Each roll-up builds its own AI, company by company, at a cost of $100M or more per platform.
AMTECH gives every portfolio company a swarm on the day of the deal, for 8% of its revenue. One deal brings dozens of businesses, and they are customers, not rivals.
General Catalyst "Creation" strategy and Long Lake: company statements and press, 2025-2026. Thrive Holdings and ADT: press reports, October 2026.

plates.head: $200,000 a year of AI inference supports a $7.6M business.
lines: Per customer, per month · Price · AI inference · Infrastructure · Customers $200K/yr covers · Revenue a year · Gross margin
End of 2027: 400 custom + 3,000 self-serve · $14K/mo · $65K/mo · 3,400 · $7.6M ARR · 87%

Inference is cheap because the swarm runs on fast open-source models. Our busiest swarm, eight teams working all week making ads, running analysis and research, building email flows and making suggestions, used about 3,000 model calls and $13 of AI a week: under $2 per team. Infrastructure runs $15 to $100 a customer, depending on workload.
Inference per customer from AMTECH's gateway, last 30 days. Revenue = customers x price x 12; gross margin after inference and infrastructure. Setup fees not included.

Our own plan reaches $98M in ARR by the end of 2029. Contractor software already proves the size: ServiceTitan and Procore are public, multi-billion-dollar companies, and Avoca reached a $1B valuation answering the phone.
